title: The right to erasure in recruiting: a practical workflow
summary: A candidate asked you to delete their data. What Article 17 requires, the one-month deadline, where candidate data hides, and a workflow that actually works.

faq.q: Do we have to delete everything when a candidate asks?
faq.a: Almost everything. Article 17 has narrow exceptions — most relevantly, data you genuinely need to establish or defend legal claims, such as evidence of a fair process within a discrimination-claim window. The exception covers that minimum, not the whole file.

faq.q: Can we prove we deleted a candidate after deleting them?
faq.a: Yes — keep an erasure log that records that a deletion happened and when, without containing the deleted personal data itself. A PII-free audit entry is compatible with the erasure it documents.

faq.q: Does erasure cover interviewer calendars and sent email?
faq.a: The right applies to personal data wherever you control it: ATS records, scheduling tools, calendar events, and mailboxes. Practically, teams delete what is reachable, and document anything that legitimately remains and why.
